title: CLAUDE.md
text: Everything mrmhub revolves around single S4 class MRMhubExperiment (R/classes.R). ’s container tibbles + processing state one experiment. Functions mostly pure-ish transforms shape mexp -> mexp — take MRMhubExperiment, return new one updated slots, flip status flags (is_istd_normalized, is_quantitated, is_filtered, is_isotope_corr, etc.). load-bearing convention — new processing functions must follow (first arg = MRMhubExperiment, return = MRMhubExperiment, update flags, never mutate dataset_orig). Functions returning bare tibble accepting raw columns break composability pipeline feel native API. Recommended pipeline order (enforced status flags, hard errors — see manual-10-design-decisions.Rmd): import_data_* → add_metadata → set_analysis_order → normalize_by_istd → correct_drift_* → correct_batch_* → quantify_by_istd / quantify_by_calibration → calc_qc_metrics → filter_features_qc → save_report_xlsx. Drift batch correction QC-sample-based (Broadhurst 2018) — never use study samples fitting. Importer family (manual-05a--importer.Rmd decision tree): import_data_mrmhub (preferred — INTEGRATOR’s long output), import_data_masshunter, import_data_skyline, import_data_csv_wide, import_data_csv_long, import_data_folder (multi-file batches). Feature variables carry _orig / _raw / _before / _beforecal / _fit postfix step overwrites . See manual-03-feature-variables.Rmd. Don’t invent new postfixes — extend existing set. Key slots (see R/classes.R full list R/mrmhub-global-definitions.R column templates): dataset_orig — long-format tibble raw imported data (one row per analysis × feature). Required cols: analysis_id, raw_data_filename, acquisition_time_stamp, feature_id. dataset — long-format working tibble metadata join + processing. Carries feature_intensity, feature_norm_intensity, feature_conc, qc_type, batch_id, etc. dataset_filtered — shape dataset, populated filter_features_qc(). annot_* — metadata tables (annot_analyses, annot_features, annot_istds, annot_responsecurves, annot_qcconcentrations, annot_studysamples, annot_batches). metrics_qc, metrics_calibration — derived QC/calibration metrics per feature. parameters_processing, status_processing — record run. var_drift_corrected, var_batch_corrected — per-variable booleans tracking feature_intensity / feature_norm_intensity / feature_conc corrected. S4 + tibbles: R/mrmhub-global-definitions.R setOldClass(c("tbl_df","tbl","data.frame")) tibbles can occupy "tbl_df" slots. Empty prototypes slot stored pkg.env$table_templates consulted class prototype import functions enforce schema. add column dataset/annot table, update matching template mrmhub-global-definitions.R downstream code silently drop mis-type .

title: Design Decisions: Why This Architecture?
text: Choice: single S4 object holds data, metadata, processing state. Rationale: Traceability — S4 object bundles original data, processed data, annotations, processing flags one place. Integrity checking — S4 validity methods ensure data metadata stay sync. Analyses accidentally deleted without updating annotations. Pipeline state — Flags like is_istd_normalized, var_drift_corrected prevent accidental double-processing. SummarizedExperiment — exports . Enforcing work QUANT exists . argument internal representation . Several parallel intensity variables obstacle — SE holds parallel assays, exactly exporter relies . experiment processed, save_dataset_summarizedexperiment() hands limma, lipidr, POMA rest ecosystem.

Produce one directly: mrmhub fills lipidr requires: Molecule feature_id, Class curated feature_class, istd is_istd, plus summarized per-assay logged / normalized flags lipidr reads validate — object missing constructs cleanly misbehaves. Using feature_class rather lipidr’s name parser also keeps class assignment correct mrmhub’s isobaric (PC 28:0|SM 32:1 M+3) neutral-loss (PE P-16:0/18:1 [-FA]) naming, lipidr parse. Use peak-area scale variable lipidr, concentrations. lipidr log-transforms log = TRUE default clamps values 1 1 first, assumes Skyline peak-area magnitudes. Concentrations µmol/L mostly 1, silently flattened log2(1) = 0 — eBayes() reports zero residual variances every fold change collapses. mrmhub warns export mostly-sub-1 assay way. cause unit scale, concentration : values nmol/L pass untouched. need concentrations, pass log = FALSE lipidr, log-transform beforehand. de_analysis() wraps limma internally returns plain data frame, LipidomicsExperiment — pipeline ends .

text: Apply normalization, quantification, drift correction, batch correction, QC filtering: Note drift correction uses study samples (ref_qc_types = "SPL") reference. Study-sample smoothing appropriate large, well-randomised sample sets; QC-based convention (Broadhurst et al. 2018) instead fits drift trend dedicated QC injections. recommended order : Normalize ISTD Quantify (ISTD external calibration) Drift correction Batch correction QC filtering See Design Decisions rationale behind order.
code: # Normalize by internal standards myexp <- normalize_by_istd(myexp) #> ! Interfering features defined in metadata, but no correction was applied. Use `correct_interferences()` to correct. #> ✔ 460 features normalized with 17 ISTDs in 499 analyses.  # Quantify using ISTD-based approach myexp <- quantify_by_istd(myexp) #> ✔ 460 feature concentrations calculated based on 42 ISTDs and sample amounts of 499 analyses. #> ℹ Concentrations are given in μmol/L.  # Correct run-order drift (Gaussian kernel, sample-based) myexp <- correct_drift_gaussiankernel(   data = myexp,   variable = "conc",   ref_qc_types = c("SPL") ) #> ℹ Applying `conc` drift correction... #> ℹ 2 feature(s) contain one or more zero or negative `conc` values. Verify your data or use `log_transform_internal = FALSE`. #> ! 1 features showed no variation in the study sample's original values across analyses.  #> ! 1 features have invalid values after smoothing. NA will be be returned for all values of these faetures. Set `use_original_if_fail = FALSE to return orginal values.. #> ! Smoothing failed for 1 feature(s) in all batches. Please check data, metadata, and fit parameters. #> ! Smoothing failed for 1 feature(s) in at least one batch: PG 36:2. Please check data, metadata and fit parameters. #> ✔ Drift correction was applied to 459 of 460 features (batch-wise). #> ℹ The median CV change of all features in study samples was -0.56% (range: -10.22% to 2.49%). The median absolute CV of all features across batches decreased from 38.96% to 38.56%.  # Correct batch effects (median centering) myexp <- correct_batch_centering(   myexp,    variable = "conc",   ref_qc_types = "SPL" ) #> ℹ Adding batch correction on top of `conc` drift-correction. #> ✔ Batch median-centering of 6 batches was applied to drift-corrected concentrations of all 502 features. #> ℹ The median CV change of all features in study samples was -0.44% (range: -27.90% to 10.30%).  The median absolute CV of all features decreased from 38.99% to 38.76%.  # Apply QC-based feature filtering myexp <- filter_features_qc(   data = myexp,   include_qualifier = FALSE,   include_istd = FALSE,    min.signalblank.median.spl.sblk = 10,   max.cv.conc.bqc = 25 ) #> Calculating feature QC metrics - please wait... #> ! The QC parameter `min.signalblank.median.spl.sblk` contains NAs for following features: LPC O-22:1, PC 34:5, PC 35:1, PG 36:2, SM 35:1|PC P_32:1 M+1, and SM 35:1|PC ....  #> These features failed QC. #> ! The QC parameter `max.cv.conc.bqc` contains NAs for following features: Cer d18:1/12:0 (ISTD) [M-H20>264], Cer d18:1/25:0 (ISTD) [M-H20>264], Hex2Cer....  #> These features failed QC. #> ✔ New feature QC filters were defined: 181 of 423 quantifier features meet QC criteria (not including the 25 quantifier ISTD features).

title: Calibration by a Reference Sample
text: Absolute re-calibration performed function calibrate_by_reference(). reference sample set via reference_sample_id. multiple analyses reference sample present dataset, either mean median calculated (defined via summarize_fun). calibrated concentration calculated : ccalibratedAnalyte=csampleAnalytecrefAnalyte×cknownAnalyte c_\text{calibrated}^\text{Analyte} = \frac{c_\text{sample}^\text{Analyte}}{c_\text{ref}^\text{Analyte}} \times c_\text{known}^\text{Analyte} re-calibrated concentrations stored variable conc , overwriting previously calculated concentrations. original concentrations, however, still available via variable conc_beforecal. re-calibrated concentrations can exported usual, also appear MRMhub XLSX report concentrations.
code: mexp_res <- calibrate_by_reference(     data = mexp,     variable = "conc",     reference_sample_id = "SRM1950",     absolute_calibration = TRUE,     batch_wise = FALSE,     summarize_fun = "mean",     undefined_conc_action = "na"   ) #> ! One or more feature concentration are not defined in the reference sample SRM1950. `NA` will be returned for these features. To change this, modify `undefined_conc_action` argument. #> ✔ 6 feature concentrations were re-calibrated using the reference sample SRM1950. #> ℹ Concentrations are given in umol/L. # Export absolute calibration concentrations save_dataset_csv(mexp, tempfile(fileext = ".csv"), variable = "conc") #> ✔ Concentration values for 65 analyses and 7 features have been exported to '/var/folders/3r/ywcsb3896zj4_0xlb_70yvlh0000gn/T//RtmpUWnOyb/file38b75a5d767a.csv'.    # Export non-calibrated concentrations save_dataset_csv(mexp_res, tempfile(fileext = ".csv"), variable = "conc_beforecal") #> ✔ Conc_beforecal values for 65 analyses and 16 features have been exported to '/var/folders/3r/ywcsb3896zj4_0xlb_70yvlh0000gn/T//RtmpUWnOyb/file38b72e0d71ef.csv'.  # Create XLSX report with calibrated concentrations as filtered dataset save_report_xlsx(mexp_res, tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx"), filtered_variable = "conc") #> Saving report to disk - please wait... #> ✔ The data processing report has been saved to '/var/folders/3r/ywcsb3896zj4_0xlb_70yvlh0000gn/T//RtmpUWnOyb/file38b774b31987.xlsx'.

title: Interference Correction
text: derive_interferences() discovers M+2 overlaps stores annot_interferences slot. Choose derivation level match acquisition: MS1 fallback MRM. MRM correction must fragment-based, heavy isotope’s contribution depends whether lands retained product ion neutral loss (Gao et al. 2021). Use level = "MS1" genuine full-scan data — never substitute MRM data missing product m/z. See manual page full rationale. default (check_coelution = TRUE) m/z-matched edge kept interferer’s peak apex falls inside victim’s integration window; chromatographically resolved pairs dropped reported. Derived factors pinned enviPat 2.8 (Loos et al. 2015) deterministic, re-importing annotation re-deriving reproduces identical edges.
code: # Class-based LC-MRM: fragment-level front/back correction (needs precursor + product m/z). mexp <- derive_interferences(mexp, level = "MRM")  # Genuine MS1 / full-scan: whole-molecule M+2 (needs precursor m/z only). # mexp <- derive_interferences(mexp, level = "MS1")

title: Interference Correction
text: correct_interferences() reads annot_interferences (unioned legacy manual annotation columns) subtracts every edge one pass: Valuecorrected=Valuetarget−∑iKi⋅Valueinterferingi \text{Value}_\text{corrected} = \text{Value}_\text{target} -    \sum_i K_i \cdot \text{Value}_{\text{interfering}_i} Upstream features chain (← B ← C) corrected first via topological ordering; circular dependencies detected aborted informative error. auto-derived edges, subtraction skipped running-corrected interferer already fallen zero, corrected values clamped zero (LICAR parity). original raw values preserved feature_intensity_orig.

text: mrmhub’s console feedback (errors, warnings, progress, metadata E/W/N validation report) deliberate, distinctive feature — gives line--line usage feedback , Quarto notebooks, instant colored summary step . value currently undermined drift ad-hoc styling across ~460 CLI call sites 36 42 R/ files: redundant second color system. cli::col_red (×206), col_yellow (×65), col_green (×54) wrap whole messages outside cli calls (cli_abort(col_red("…")), cli_alert_info(col_yellow("…"))). cli_abort already red, cli_alert_warning yellow, cli_alert_success green — wrapping redundant, prevents theming, makes color fragile Quarto. concept styled three ways — column/feature-variable names {.field} (×7) vs {.var} (×5) vs backticks-inside-col_*(); argument names {.arg} (×19) vs "Argument \x`“insidecol_red`. Redundant/unsafe glue::glue() nested inside cli calls (cli already interpolates {}), including empty cli_abort(glue::glue("")) classes.R. Inconsistent message structure — single strings vs color-wrapped vs idiomatic named-bullet vectors; subset uses x//!/v bullets. Leftover base R messaging — stop()/warning()/cat()/message() helper.R, tibble-classes.R, plot-featureprofile.R, calc-eda.R, data-example.R, plus ad-hoc message("  done!") + \r progress plot-runscatter.R, plot-qc-correlations.R, data-export.R, qc-filtering.R (natural cli_progress_* candidates — none used today). cli theme, .onLoad, options(cli.*) — nothing configures color non-interactive (Quarto) rendering. Errors collapse traceback. validation-report aborts pass trace = NULL, hiding backtrace, call handling inconsistent — users always tell function raised error. reported numbers wrong (just mis-styled). count audit found several messages whose interpolated number measure sentence claims (metadata-row counts sold “feature concentrations re-calibrated”, -dataset denominators, non-intersected exclusion counts). wrong number silently misleads way bad styling never — highest-value fix. transforms give feedback . exported mexp→mexp steps run silently success — importantly core pipeline verb calc_qc_metrics() — user can’t tell step ran . Input validation ad hoc. ’s shared entry guard (check_data) column guard (check_var_in_dataset), shared “required arg / right type / valid value” helper, several exported functions accept missing wrong args fail later obscure @/“object found” error instead friendly one.

what: Critical review — scope discipline (keep it lean, low-risk)
title: Plan: Standardize & correct all CLI console output in mrmhub
text: self-review R/tidyverse maintainer. plan first drafted -reaches several places; value real concentrated workstreams, risk concentrated others. Adjustments: Sequence independent, individually-shippable commits — one 42-file big-bang (unreviewable, huge blast radius, every reworded message breaks text-matching test). Recommended order value ÷ risk: 1. F — numeric correctness (highest value, isolated, pre-existing bugs unrelated styling). Caveat: fix changes reported count, need domain judgment (e.g. analyses denominator include blanks?). Treat propose fix + confirm intended semantics maintainer, silent unilateral change. Ship commit. 2. D (E/W/N report) + G (calc_qc_metrics) — contained, user-visible wins. 3. + B — colour relocation (wrappers) + Quarto rendering mechanism (see revision). 4. J — manual-11-quarto-workflows guide + generate_workflow_qmd() alignment (depends B’s colour setup settled, since page scaffold embed ). 5. C + — styling sweep + truncation/retrievability — largest churn, lowest per-change value; last, mechanically. 6. H — validation, minimal (see revision). De-scoped avoid -engineering: - : use lightweight internal wrapper helpers, global cli theme. Registering options(cli.theme = …) .onLoad clobbers user’s (packages’) theme whole session — anti-pattern. since chosen look full-line color, col_*() mechanism, redundancy — relocating color, deleting . internal helpers (mh_success/mh_info/mh_warn/mh_danger) apply col_*() reproduce today’s look exactly, stay local, add zero global state, trivial maintain. Drop zzz.R theme registration. - Error policy: fix sites actually break — handful passing trace = NULL (metadata-import report aborts). mass-edit ~279 aborts set call =; cli_abort() already infers caller correctly almost everywhere. - Drop cli:: namespacing normalization wholesale base-R→cli migration — cosmetic, high churn, low value. Leave legitimate cat()/print() S3 print/format methods (tibble-classes.R) alone. - Defer cli_progress_* conversion — new behavior non-interactive/Quarto edge cases; ad-hoc message("done") works outside correctness/consistency ask. - {.field} vs {.var} unification: KEPT dedicated pass (maintainer chose full class consistency) — standardize column/feature-variable names {.field} across sites. Accept extra test churn uniform end state. - Removing nested glue::glue(): valuable blind — confirm string uses glue-feature deleting wrapper; keep glue_collapse et al. - H stays minimal & idiomatic: lean ’s free — arg_match() already emits “mean” enums; check_data() already guards object. build fuzzy-match/validation framework (drop agrepl “mean” helper). Add high-impact guards (data_sum_features→check_data; add_metadata type; smooth_fun enum; save_*(path) scalar; 2 numeric-positive checks otherwise fail cryptically). Skip ~35 filter thresholds. permissive types. New guards can break loose--valid existing calls — add guard test, run suite. - G: calc_qc_metrics (core, stable) now; defer detect_outlier_pca / data_sum_features — flagged experimental/-revision; low ROI polish. Guiding rule: change message’s wording buys correctness clarity — pure style — keep test churn (real hidden cost) risk bounded.

what: Canonical styling conventions (the source of truth for the pass)
title: Plan: Standardize & correct all CLI console output in mrmhub
text: Language & grammar rules: sentence case; alerts concise trailing period unless multi-sentence; aborts/warnings full sentences periods bullet structure; uniform validation phrasing "{.arg x} must {.val } {.val b}."; fix grammar bugs (e.g. "must larger 0" → "must greater 0"); consistent domain nouns (feature, analysis, QC type, batch). Rewrite unclear / ungrammatical / badly-punctuated messages clarity. Length directional, absolute: default shortening (drop filler like “Please verify … try ” bullet already says ); message genuinely -informative — missing information user needs understand act — add information even lengthens, concise phrasing. (Namespacing normalization base-R→cli migration scope — see Scope discipline.) Message-layout discipline (avoid ragged multi-line output): - Success/info summaries single-line — one mh_success()/mh_info() (=one cli_alert_*) call, embedded \n, bullet vectors. cli soft-wraps long line console width aligned hanging indent (tidy), length ≠ mess; shorten rule keeps wrapping much anyway. - Multi-line bullet blocks (c(headline, "x"=…, ""=…)) cli_abort/cli_warn — extra context earns vertical space. Cap ~3–4 bullets; use bullet form routine success messages. - Delete existing messiness sources: manual \n strings, multi-line glue::glue(), ad-hoc cat()/\r+"done!" progress (removed sweep). - Long lists stay one (wrapped) line via §truncation — never dozens lines. - intentional multi-line block E/W/N report, unified §D. - Keep summaries short don’t soft-wrap awkwardly narrow PDF/HTML column; manual-11 setup chunk documents sane options(width). Efficiency rules: remove nested glue::glue() inside cli (carefully — glue-feature used); use {?s} / cli::qty() / cli::() counts instead ifelse; use vector collapsing instead manual paste(collapse=). (cli_progress_* conversion deferred — see Scope discipline.)

title: Derive isotopic interference relationships — derive_interferences
text: Automatically discovers isotopic (M+2) interference relationships measured features stores annot_interferences slot, ready correct_interferences(). Two levels supported: "MRM" (default): fragment-based front/back correction class-based LC-MRM data, derived LICAR method (see manual). Requires precursor product m/z mrm_pattern per feature. "MS1": whole-molecule M+2 correction MS1 / full-scan acquisitions. factor M+2 relative abundance species' molecular formula; interfering pairs matched precursor m/z (~2 Da apart) within feature class. Requires precursor m/z .

title: RunScatter plot — plot_runscatter
text: runscatter function visualizes raw processed feature signals across different sample/QC types along analysis sequence. helps identify trends, detect outliers, assess analytical performance. Available feature variables, retention time (RT) full width half maximum (FWHM), can plotted analysis order timestamps. default, QC types present dataset plotted. QC types predefined colors shapes assigned black shapes. User-defined QC types predefined colors shapes mrmhub. assigned black shapes. predefined color shape, assigned shapes black. show specific QC types use qc_types argument. plot feature values last applied drift/batch correction, add *_before variable name, e.g., intensity_before conc_before. plot uncorrected feature values (drift/batch correction), add *_raw variable name, e.g., intensity_raw conc_raw. show corresponding fit curves, set show_trend = TRUE. function also supports visualizing analysis batches, reference lines (mean \(\pm\) SD), trends. offers customization options display batch separators, apply outlier capping, show smoothed trend curves, add reference lines, incorporate features. Outlier capping particularly useful focus QC study sample trends might otherwise obscured extreme values high variability. runscatter function serves central QC tool workflow, providing critical insights data quality.

Features rows analyses columns, following SummarizedExperiment convention. feature variable becomes one assay, feature_intensity, feature_norm_intensity feature_conc sit side--side object addressed SummarizedExperiment::assay(se, "conc"). Assay names drop feature_ prefix. annot_features becomes rowData(), annot_analyses becomes colData(), processing state (status, flags, concentration unit) becomes metadata(). Everything exported. Internal standards, QC samples, blanks calibrants included flagged rather dropped, downstream tools need : lipidr requires istd annotation pmp's blank filter needs blanks present. Norm_Intensity_FullDataset: Normalized feature intensities full, non-filtered dataset. SampleMetadata:  Analysis metadata imported used processing steps FeatureMetadata: Feature metadata imported used processing steps InternalStandards: Internal standards metadata concentrations BatchInfo: Information batches positions first last analysis/sample batch certain data sets available, function includes empty tables corresponding dataset. title: mrmhub 0.9.2
text: New save_dataset_mztab() writes processed MRMhubExperiment HUPO-PSI mzTab-M 2.0.0-M standard format (format expected repositories MetaboLights). analysis becomes assay, feature Small Molecule Feature (SMF) row grouped Small Molecule Summary (SML) rows analyte. abundance variable selectable via variable (default "conc", fall-back raw intensity unquantified data), metadata header can enriched instrument, contact publication. Output validator-passing official LIFS mzTab-M validator. New import_data_mztab() imports mzTab-M files produced tools (e.g. Lipid Data Analyzer, MS-DIAL, MZmine). SMF becomes feature assay analysis; per-assay abundances imported feature_intensity, feature identities study_variable grouping (batch_id) carried available. directions pure R add runtime dependency. See Import & Export mzTab-M recipe article.

what: Handling of analytical sequence gaps in plot_runscatter() and plot_rla_boxplot()
title: mrmhub 0.9.2
text: functions gain following new arguments handle gaps analytical sequence: remove_gaps — TRUE, gaps data (mainly caused unannotated analysis results) removed indicated vertical lines index labels. gap lines can customised via gap_line_color, gap_line_width, gap_label_size, gap_scale. collapse_excluded — TRUE, gaps x-axis caused QC types selected collapsed. useful plotting samples subset QC types.

what: Support for long feature names in plot_runscatter() and plot_responsecurves()
title: mrmhub 0.9.2
text: label_wrap label_wrap_width allow long feature_id strip labels wrapped across multiple lines. Set label_wrap = TRUE enable wrapping; use label_wrap_width control maximum line width characters (default: 25).

what: Plotting multiple response curves per feature in plot_responsecurves()
title: mrmhub 0.9.2
text: plot_responsecurves() gains following new arguments: curve_layout — one "overlay", "rows", "cols". "overlay" plots curves panel; "rows" splits curve separate row features columns; "cols" splits curve separate column features rows. Use fixed_scale_curves = TRUE fix y-axis upper limit maximum value across curves feature. r2_vstep — adjusts vertical spacing R² labels different curves curve_layout = "overlay".
